newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan post ministry plans ATM linkup with Citibank.
newsitem.headline: Japan post ministry plans ATM linkup with Citibank.

text.p: Japan's Posts and Telecommunications Ministry said on Tuesday that it plans to connect its on-line system for automated teller machines (ATMs) and cash dispensers with Citibank offices in Japan.

The ministry has made a budget request for the next fiscal year starting April 1 for funds to link the system, and the plan will depend on whether the budget request gets passed, a ministry spokesman said.
He quoted Posts and Telecommunications Minister Ichiro Hino as saying that the link would bring added convenience to consumers.
A Citibank spokesman said that the U.S. bank had asked the ministry for permission to link up with nearly 23,000 ATMs operated by post offices across Japan.

The link would allow Citibank customers to deposit and withdraw funds and check their account balances at the post offices' ATMs, and allow individuals with savings accounts at post offices to do the same at Citibank terminals.
Financial industry sources said Citibank's planned link-up would be the first alliance between government-run post offices and a private-sector bank.

But the sources said Japanese banks have voiced concern that their business will be gradually taken away by the government-run postal savings system. Private-sector banks have complained about unfair competition from the government-run system.

In a separate move, the ministry has asked securities houses to link up with ATMs at post offices in order to allow post office savings account holders to buy and sell stocks through ATMs, they said. However, brokers have been cautious about the move, they said.
